description: PARTIAL SAVE: writes ONLY the 'Character' field of TitlePublicConfigurationModel; all other v1/v2 fields stay untouched. Character/hero catalogue — playable units, NPCs, summons. Defines stats, abilities, evolution/level-up paths, art/asset references. Distinct from Item (generic inventory) — characters typically have progression and abilities. Skins (alternative looks) live per character in Skins.Definitions, and each skin IS a non-stackable, non-expiring Item from the Item section (Skins.Definitions.<id>.Item) — create that item first; any system that grants items (Store offers, lootboxes, season, quests, rewards) then grants the skin, and Item.Stats, if set, count toward Power like gear.

CharacterClassification.description: Classification / categorical metadata. All fields are string IDs referencing external catalogs (no inline catalogs). Each field is optional — leave empty for systems the title does not use.

RarityID.description: Rarity identifier (e.g. "Common", "Rare", "Epic", "Legendary"). Same pattern as ItemMetadata.RarityID.

Tags.description: Free-form gameplay tags (e.g. "ranged", "flying", "event-2026"). Useful for UI filters and quest/lootbox targeting.

CharacterDefinition.description: One character template (hero) in the title catalog. Self-contained: identity, classification, unlock, equipment rules, stats, levels.

CharacterID.description: Unique character ID. Reserved value "Main" denotes the always-available primary character. Must not contain '.' or '$' (MongoDB path restriction).

Presets.description: Container of character preset wiring (stats / levels / equipment). All blocks merge with inline by key (preset base + inline override/add + Remove): Stats by StatID, Levels by level key, Equipment by SlotID inside Slots. Missing/invalid PresetID = no preset. null = presets unused. Resolved by CharacterConfigResolver.

RankLadder.description: Shape of the rank ladder: how many ranks and how the upgrade price grows. Empty = taken from the levels preset; empty there too = the previous path, where every rank is described by the Levels dictionary.

RankStatCurve.description: Curve of the GLOBAL stat multiplier over the character's rank: it applies to every stat at once, on top of the per-stat StatDefinition.RankCurve. The step is the rank (numbered from 1); leave Base empty, the curve is read as a multiplier. Empty = rank alone does not change stats. Replaces the former per-rank multiplier, whose neutral value was 1 rather than empty. Arbitrary per-rank values are written as Shape=Table (one point per rank); even growth as Shape=PerStepRate — multipliers 1.0/1.2/1.4 at ranks 1..3 are PerStepRate = 0.2.

Skins.description: Character skins (alternative looks). A skin is an ITEM from Item.Catalogs: owning a skin means owning a copy of that item, wearing it binds that copy to the reserved equipment slot "@skin". Any system that grants items (Store, Lootbox, Season, Quest, Reward, manual grants) therefore grants skins too. If the item has Stats they count toward Power like gear; without Stats the skin is purely cosmetic. null = the character has no skins.

StatMaxLevelCurve.description: Curve of the stat-upgrade CAP over the character's rank. The base is each stat's StatDefinition.MaxLevel, the step is the rank (numbered from 1). Empty = rank does not raise the cap. Replaces the former per-rank cap multiplier. Read in exactly one place — CharacterConfigResolver.EffectiveStatMaxLevel.

Stats.description: Per-character upgradable stat directory. Key is StatID. null/empty = no upgradable stats. Fully self-contained — no global fallback.

CharacterEquipment.description: Equipment rules for the character. Per-slot configuration with character-level gates, stat prerequisites and item filters. Validated in addition to the item-side ItemEquipment rules.

Slots.description: Per-slot equipment rules. Key is SlotID. A character can equip into a slot iff it has an entry here — absence = slot forbidden.

CharacterEquipmentSlot.description: Equip rules for one slot on one character. All gates must pass: character must satisfy unlock/stat gates, and the item must satisfy rarity/tag/level filters. Validated in addition to ItemEquipment rules on the item side.

AllowedItemTags.description: Item must have at least one of these tags (matches ItemDefinition.Tags). null/empty = no tag filter.

AllowedRarityIDs.description: Allowed item rarity IDs (matches ItemMetadata.RarityID). null/empty = any rarity.

MaxItemLevel.description: Maximum allowed item-instance level in this slot. 0 = no upper bound. Compared against UnstackableItemInstanceState.Level (per-instance).

MinCharacterLevel.description: Minimum character Level required to use this slot. 0 = always available.

MinItemLevel.description: Minimum allowed item-instance level in this slot. 0 = no lower bound. Compared against UnstackableItemInstanceState.Level (per-instance, upgraded via ItemV2.UpgradeLevel).

StatRequirements.description: Stat-level prerequisites the character must meet to use the slot. Reuses StatRequirement.

CharacterIdentity.description: Identity / display metadata of a character. All assets live in AssetPaths only — there are no separate IconPath fields.

AssetPaths.description: Named asset references (e.g. "icon", "portrait", "fullArt", "sprite", "voiceIntro"). This is the only place asset paths live.

DisplayName.description: Display name shown in UI (localized or base).

Lore.description: Optional long-form lore / backstory for character detail screens.

SortOrder.description: Display order in roster UI. Lower values are listed first.

CharacterPresetBindings.description: Container of character preset wiring — one PresetBinding per block. Inline data (Stats/Levels/Equipment) lives on CharacterDefinition. All blocks merge by key (Stats=StatID, Levels=level, Equipment=SlotID). null = presets unused.

Equipment.description: Equipment preset binding (merge by SlotID inside Slots).

Levels.description: Levels preset binding (merge by level key).

CharacterPresetRegistry.description: Container of character preset registries. Each field is a dictionary keyed by PresetID. Resolved at read-time via CharacterConfigResolver over PresetResolver.

Equipment.description: Reusable equipment-rule sets keyed by PresetID.

Levels.description: Reusable level/rank sets keyed by PresetID.

Stats.description: Reusable stat sets keyed by PresetID.

CharacterRankLadder.description: The rank ladder: how many ranks there are and how the upgrade price grows. This is the ONLY source of rank prices — there is no per-rank dictionary. A non-uniform ladder is expressed by the curve shape (Table / TableAbsolute place a multiplier per rank). What the ladder cannot express is a different price COMPOSITION per rank: the composition is fixed by PriceOptions and the curve only scales the amount.

CostCurve.description: Price growth over the rank. The base is the price in PriceOptions and the step is the rank, with FirstPaidRank counting as the first step. Empty = the same price at every rank. Leave Base empty.

FirstPaidRank.description: First PAID rank. Ranks below it are free. Empty = 1, i.e. the first rank is already paid. This exists for activation: rank 0 means an inactive character, and the 0 -> 1 step is free in most titles because the character itself is paid for in CharacterUnlock.PriceOptions.

MaxRank.description: How many ranks the character has in total. Empty = the ceiling stays the highest rank present in the Levels dictionary (the previous behaviour).

PriceOptions.description: Base upgrade price — the price of the first PAID rank (see FirstPaidRank). Higher ranks are scaled by CostCurve. A store-paid option is not allowed: the upgrade spans a range of ranks and is merged into one total, while a receipt pays for exactly one SKU.

Identity.description: Display name, description, sort order and look of the skin. AssetPaths here is the look ON the character (model, portrait); the item's own AssetPaths is its inventory icon.

Item.description: The item that IS this skin. Must be a non-stackable item without an expiration: a worn copy is bound to the character and protected from sale, NFT withdrawal and expiry. null is allowed only for the entry named by DefaultSkinID.

Requirements.description: Requirements to WEAR the skin. They gate wearing only; owning is never gated.

Sale.description: Direct sale from the character screen (Character/UnlockSkin). null = not sold directly — the skin comes only from other systems (Store offer, lootbox, season, quest, reward, manual grant).

SkinID.description: Unique skin ID within the character. Empty = the dictionary key. Not stored in player state: the worn skin is identified by its item.

CharacterSkinItem.description: Reference to the item that is the skin.

CatalogID.description: Catalog of the item. Empty = resolved by ItemID when the item lives in exactly one catalog.

ItemID.description: Item ID. Must not contain '.' or '$'.

CharacterSkinRequirements.description: Requirements to wear a skin — the same axes as an equipment slot.

MinCharacterLevel.description: Minimum character Level (rank) to wear the skin. 0 = none.

StatRequirements.description: Stat-level prerequisites to wear the skin. Reuses StatRequirement.

CharacterSkinSale.description: Direct sale of a skin from the character screen. Schedule and Gate restrict BUYING only — a skin the player already owns can always be worn.

Gate.description: Audience allowed to buy. null = everyone.

PriceOptions.description: Ways to pay. Dictionary key = PriceOption.OptionID. null/empty = not sold directly (granted by other systems only). An explicit option with an empty Cost is a free claim, limited by ownership.

Schedule.description: Sale window. null = always on sale.

CharacterSkins.description: Skins block of a character: the catalog of alternative looks plus the base look.

DefaultSkinID.description: SkinID of the base look: an entry of Definitions WITHOUT Item. UI-only — equipping it is the same as removing the worn skin. null = the base look is the character's own Identity.AssetPaths.

Definitions.description: Skin catalog of this character. Key is SkinID; an empty SkinID field is taken from the key. Must not contain '.' or '$'.

PriceOptions.description: Ways to pay for unlocking this character. Dictionary key = PriceOption.OptionID. null/empty = cannot be unlocked through a cost (must be granted by other systems).

UnlockedByDefault.description: If true, the character is available without any unlock action. "Main" must have this set to true. Other characters typically default to false and rely on Cost or external grants (lootbox/quest reward).

x-enum-descriptions: Platform was not reported, or the reported one contradicts the request fingerprint.
Browser: web build, WebGL, or a messenger mini-app.
Android build (Google Play Billing).
iOS / iPadOS build (App Store, StoreKit).
Step: hold the previous point's value until the next one. Behaviour of an unset field.
Linear between adjacent points.
Geometric between adjacent points: lo * (hi/lo)^t.

CurvePoint.description: One breakpoint of a table curve.

AtStep.description: Step (level / rank / stage) at which this point takes effect. Empty = the point is ignored.

Value.description: Value at this point. Empty = the point is ignored.

x-enum-descriptions: Value does not change with the step. Same behaviour as an unset curve.
Additive in the value's own units: base + PerStep * (step - firstStep).
Additive share of the base: base * (1 + PerStepRate * (step - firstStep)). 0.1 = +10% of base per step.
Compounding: base * (1 + GrowthRate)^(step - firstStep).
Table of multipliers over the base: base * interpolate(Points, step).
Table of absolute values: interpolate(Points, step). The base is ignored.

CyclicSchedule.description: Calendar-aligned cycles with reset. Unified replacement of LeaderboardScheduleMode.Cyclic + LeaderboardCycleReset.

AnchorUtc.description: FixedInterval only: anchor instant (coerced to UTC, used as-is including time-of-day) from which IntervalSeconds windows are counted; the anchor defines alignment. null/unset = 2026-01-01 00:00 UTC. Ignored for calendar resets.

ClaimGraceHours.description: Grace window (hours) after cycle end to claim previous-cycle rewards. 0 = current cycle only.

IntervalSeconds.description: FixedInterval only: window length in SECONDS (e.g. 86400 = 1 day, 21600 = 6 hours, 864000 = 10 days). default = 86400 (1 day). Ignored for calendar resets.

PauseBetweenCyclesSec.description: FixedInterval only: pause (SECONDS) between active windows. 0 = back-to-back. When >0 the cycle 'pulses': active for IntervalSeconds, then a pause of this length (inactive during the pause — CanEarn=false/IsInPause), then the next window. Full period = IntervalSeconds + PauseBetweenCyclesSec. Ignored for calendar resets (they are gapless by definition).

EquipmentPreset.description: Shared, reusable equipment-rule set. Stored in CharacterDefinitions.Presets.Equipment by PresetID. Wraps the same CharacterEquipment used inline.

Equipment.description: Preset equipment rules (per-slot). Same shape as CharacterDefinition.Equipment.

EventTokenAddress.description: Universal event-token address. Uniquely identifies the system and event the tokens belong to.

EntityID.description: Event identifier within the system. In TITLE CONFIG (rewards written by a designer or an AI agent) scheduled systems use the SHORT form — the cycle number is unknowable at config time: "{TimedEventID}" / "{LeaderboardID}" = whichever instance is active at grant time, or "{ID}:{ChainedEventID}" = that chain phase in the current cycle. The engine (EventTokenAddressResolver in ResourceService) expands it before granting; a grant with no active instance is dropped. At RUNTIME the bucket address is always the full form "{EntityID}:{InstanceKey}": TimedEvent Scheduled → "{TimedEventID}:s{yyyyMMddHHmm}"; TimedEvent Chain → "{chainID}:{cycleIndex}:{chainedEventID}"; Leaderboard → "{leaderboardID}:{instanceKey}"; CoopEvent → CoopChainID; Season → SeasonChainID.

EventTokenOperation.description: Information about granted event tokens. Returned in Board_Roll, QuestComplete and other responses. All multipliers (Roll/Premium/BonusWindow/ProgressiveTier/SeasonBuffs) are applied via ModifierService before ResourceService; this carries the final amount. Use ModifierApplyResult alongside ResourceOperation if UI needs multiplier breakdown.

Address.description: Event token address — where to grant or consume.

Amount.description: Token amount — how many to grant or consume.

Source.description: Operation source (sourceKey used for analytics and limits).

x-enum-descriptions: Landing on an EventToken tile on the board.
Passing start (GO) on the board.
Successful board attack.
Successful board raid.
Building or repairing a structure on the board.
Completing a board stage.

Completing a board Special mode — either via Instant choice or via Claim after the Timed window. Post-resolution source (mirrors BoardAttack/BoardRaid): fires at the final Special reward grant, separately from BoardTileLanding (which fires on the actual tile landing during Roll).
Completing a quest.
Store purchase.
Daily login.
Referral invite.
Token grant as a reward for a milestone or streak in another event. Server-only source — the client cannot invoke it directly.
Arbitrary action — the developer calls the server API with ActionName in Params.
Marketplace (v2) sale — deal settlement on the seller side. Server-only source. Filter Params: CatalogID / ItemID / OfferType.
Marketplace (v2) purchase — deal settlement on the buyer side. Server-only source. Filter Params: CatalogID / ItemID / OfferType.
In-game currency spend — any scenario where a resource operation actually consumed currency. Server-only source. The multiplier equals the amount spent. Filter Params: CurrencyID.
Opening a lootbox/chest. Server-only source. The multiplier equals how many boxes were opened in the call. Filter Params: LootboxID.

Real-money store purchase (IAP). Server-only source: fired in PurchaseV2 AFTER the receipt is verified and rewards are granted. The multiplier equals the number of product units granted. Filter Params: ProductID, Store. Deliberately separate from StorePurchase, which covers in-game currency spending.
Crypto deposit credited to the in-game balance. Multiplier is 1 (one operation). Filter Params: CurrencyID, NetworkID.
Crypto withdrawal CONFIRMED on chain. Multiplier is 1 (one operation). Filter Params: CurrencyID, NetworkID.
Spending crypto currency in-game. The multiplier equals the amount spent. Filter Params: CurrencyID.

In-game currency GRANT — mirror of CurrencySpent. The multiplier equals the amount granted, so ScaleWithRollMultiplier picks the meaning: "earn N currency" or "receive currency N times". Filter Params: CurrencyID and Origin ("Gameplay" | "RewardClaim"), the latter separating gameplay earnings from reward payouts — without it a goal like "earn N" would be closed by another quest's reward.
CRYPTO currency GRANT in-game (wallet deposits are NOT included — that is CryptoDeposit). The multiplier equals the amount granted. Filter Params: CurrencyID, Origin.

Leaderboard ScoreSources only: the board accepts the NUMBER the game submits itself (SubmitScore / SubmitScoresBatch). Not an event — it grants nothing and matches nothing, it only allows. Without it the board refuses a score from the game: an empty ScoreSources list means the board is not set up. Caps live in Limits: PerActivationCap = max score of ONE submission, DailyCap / DailyWeightCap = submissions / total score per UTC day, CooldownSeconds, MaxPerWindow + WindowSeconds, TotalCap = submissions for all time. A submission over a cap is refused, not trimmed. BaseWeight is not read. Set caps the game can really reach: the client is not trusted, they are the only limit on a forged score.

ExperimentVariantCondition.description: Experiment-variant membership condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. The gate passes if the player is assigned to one of Variants of experiment ExperimentID (empty list = just enrolled). A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: make two configs (offer A, offer B), each gated to its variant.

ExperimentID.description: Experiment ID whose assignment is checked.

Variants.description: Allowed variants (any-of). Empty = being assigned to any variant is enough (enrolled). A player with no assignment for this experiment does NOT pass.

LevelsPreset.description: Shared, reusable rank ladder. Stored in CharacterDefinitions.Presets.Levels by PresetID. There is no per-rank dictionary: ranks are described by one ladder.

RankLadder.description: Rank-ladder shape of the preset. Overridden by the character's inline RankLadder.

LimitSpec.description: Unified anti-farm limits ("how much / how often"). Replaces TriggerLimits (Scheduling), DealNodeLimitsDefinition (DealOffer), StoreOfferRules caps (Store) and ClaimRewardDefinition sliding fields (Reward). 0 on an axis = no limit. Superset of axes with DIFFERENT enforcement semantics: DailyCap/DailyWeightCap = calendar UTC day; MaxPerWindow/WindowSeconds = sliding window. Usually one set is filled per system, the rest = 0. Counters are stored/enforced by each system; this is config thresholds only.

DailyCap.description: Cap on triggers/actions per calendar day (UTC). 0 = no limit.

DailyWeightCap.description: Cap on weight (e.g. token amount) per calendar day (UTC). 0 = no limit.

MaxPerWindow.description: Sliding window: max triggers within WindowSeconds. 0 = disabled.

PerActivationCap.description: Cap within a single activation/session. 0 = no limit.

TotalCap.description: Lifetime cap per user. 0 = no limit.

WindowSeconds.description: Sliding-window length (seconds). Used only when MaxPerWindow > 0.

PremiumTierBundle.description: Per-tier bundle describing a structurally different set of resources (different ItemIDs/tokens/currencies) available only to subscribers. Used in both ResourceGrant.PremiumTiers (rewards) and ResourceConsume.PremiumTiers (price). Differs from PremiumTierBonus/PremiumTierDiscount which only modify Standard Amounts by percentage.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

Resources.description: Items, currencies and tokens of this tier. Entries with Amount=0 are valid and mean 'skip'. Empty/null Resources in Consume.PremiumTiers means 'premium pays nothing' (equivalent to Discounts: 1.0).

PremiumTierDiscount.description: Percentage discount on ResourceConsume.Standard for a premium tier. All Standard Amounts are multiplied by (1 - Discount) with Math.Ceiling rounding in player's favor. Applies only to Standard; ignored if PremiumTiers matches. Best matching tier wins, discounts do not stack. Symmetric to PremiumTierBonus.

Discount.description: Discount as a SHARE: 0.1 = -10%, 1.0 = free. Empty or 0 = no discount. The unit is the same across the whole platform — never a 0..100 percent.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum tier required to qualify for this modifier.

RequiredPremiumID.description: Optional specific subscription ID. null = any subscription matching MinPremiumTier.

PresetBinding.description: Wiring for one preset block of an entity: a reference into the module's preset registry + optional keys to drop. Reusable Core container, one per preset-able block, held inside the entity's Presets container. Replaces the former scattered flat *PresetID / *Remove fields. Combination is data-driven, no mode (PresetResolver): no PresetID -> inline only; preset + empty inline -> preset; preset + inline -> merge (preset base + inline overrides/adds by key), Remove drops keys. For a single object (Character Equipment) there is nothing to key-merge, so inline wins when both are present.

PresetID.description: Preset key in the module registry (e.g. LeaderboardDefinitions.Presets.Milestones[PresetID]). Empty/null = preset unused (inline layer only).

Remove.description: Keys removed from the merged result. Dictionary key for dictionaries; element key for keyed lists (Rank / SlotID / RuleID). null = remove nothing. Ignored when no preset is set.

PriceOption.description: A single way to pay for an entity. Platform-wide standard: everything with a configured price describes it as a PriceOptions dictionary whose key is the OptionID. Options exist because ResourceConsume.Standard is charged as a whole (AND), while a price across platforms is a choice (OR): a store SKU on mobile, a token on web. Platform duties split as "the client renders, the server allows": title config ships as one immutable artifact per (version, field set), so it cannot be filtered per request — the client hides options by AllowedPlatforms, while PriceOptionSelector.Select refuses a charge whose option is not available on the caller's platform.

AllowedPlatforms.description: Platforms this option is available on. Empty/null = all of them. Do not list Unknown: a client that did not report its platform only gets options with no platform restriction, i.e. those safe everywhere.

AssetPaths.description: Option assets (currency icon, discount badge). Key = asset slug.

Cost.description: What is charged for this option. Standard is the base; PremiumDiscounts / PremiumTiers behave as everywhere else. An entry of type Purchase means the option is paid in a store rather than with a player resource: the payment is verified before ResourceService and never enters the resource operation. No initializer on purpose — "unset" must differ from "set to empty"; an unset Cost means the option is free.

Name.description: Display name of the option ("For gold", "$0.99"). A localization key or a literal — resolved client-side by the rule own table → fallback table → the key itself.

OptionID.description: Payment-option identifier. If empty, the dictionary key is substituted (PriceOptionResolver) — the client selects an option by this ID, so an option without one would be unselectable.

RelativeWindow.description: Window defined RELATIVE to the parent instance's start (see ScheduleMode.Relative). Window start = parent.StartUtc + OffsetSecondsFromParentStart. End = start + DurationSeconds, or (if DurationSeconds <= 0) the parent's end; never extends past the parent's end. Lets one config auto-repeat: sub-entity dates are computed from the current parent instance instead of being written absolutely.

AllowEarningAfterEnd.description: Whether progress can still be earned after the window ends (until grace ends). Default false.

ClaimGraceHours.description: Grace window (hours) after the window ends for claiming rewards. Default 0.

DurationSeconds.description: Window length in SECONDS. 0 (or less) = the window lasts until the parent's end (typical for "stage opens and stays until the event ends"). >0 = lasts exactly that long (but never longer than the parent).

OffsetSecondsFromParentStart.description: Window start offset in SECONDS from the parent instance start. 0 = open immediately with the parent. E.g. "Day N" = (N-1) * 86400.

ResourceBundle.description: Set of items, currencies and tokens for a single operation direction (grant only or consume only).

ResourceConsume.description: Consume direction container for ResourceOperation. Two mutually exclusive premium mechanisms over Standard: PremiumTiers (priority) replaces Standard with the best matching tier's Resources via Replace, and PremiumDiscounts (fallback) applies a percentage discount to Standard only when no PremiumTier matched. Best matching tier wins, no stacking.

PremiumDiscounts.description: Percentage discount on Standard for premium players. Single best matching tier wins (no stacking): Amount = ceil(Amount * (1 - Discount)). Ignored if any PremiumTier matched — Replace takes over.

PremiumTiers.description: Structurally different price for premium players (different ItemID/CurrencyID/Target). Always Replace, single best matching tier wins. If matched, Standard is fully replaced and PremiumDiscounts is ignored; otherwise fallback to Standard + PremiumDiscounts.

Standard.description: Base — what to charge all players including F2P.

ResourceEntry.description: Universal container for a single entry in a resource bundle (item or currency). The set of populated fields depends on Type: Item uses CatalogID/ItemID/Amount; VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency uses CurrencyID/Amount; Purchase uses only ProductID (paid in a store).

Amount.description: Amount of the resource. Used by every type except Purchase, where the quantity is decided by the store itself and this field is ignored. Amount=0 is valid in Consume.PremiumTiers and means 'do not charge'.

AmountUsd.description: CryptoCurrency only: the amount in USD instead of a token count. At the moment of the operation the engine converts it to tokens at the LIVE market price of the token (charge: rounded up to a whole token; grant: rounded down). When set, Amount is ignored; the operation result carries the converted Amount.

CatalogID.description: Item catalog identifier. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs (e.g. "main", "season").

CurrencyID.description: Currency identifier. Used only when Type is VirtualCurrency or CryptoCurrency. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies or cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

ItemID.description: Item identifier within the catalog. Used only when Type is Item. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Item.Catalogs[Catalog].Items.

ProductID.description: IAP product identifier. Used only when Type is Purchase. Corresponds to a key in cfg.Purchase.Products — OUR stable product ID, not the store SKU (per-store SKUs live in IapProductDefinition.StoreProductIDs).

Type.description: Resource type. Determines which fields must be populated: Item (catalog item), VirtualCurrency (off-chain), CryptoCurrency (on-chain), or Purchase (real-money payment in a store).

x-enum-descriptions: Catalog item. Requires CatalogID, ItemID and Amount.
In-game (off-chain) virtual currency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.VirtualCurrencies.
On-chain cryptocurrency. Requires CurrencyID and Amount. Looked up in cfg.Currency.CryptoCurrencies.

Real-money payment in a store. Requires only ProductID (a product from cfg.Purchase.Products); the amount and currency are decided by the store from the SKU price tier. NOT a storable resource and never passes through ResourceService — the money is paid outside before the server learns about it, so the entry is consumed by the receipt check (ExternalPaymentGate) and stripped before the resource operation. Allowed only in Consume and only for Consumable products.

Rewarded-video credit. One credit equals one verified ad view that can be spent in systems requiring rewarded video (lootbox open, reward double, re-roll, booster). Granted +1 per server-verified view, or as N from milestones/quests/premium perks; spent -1 per gated action.

Payment in Coin, the PLATFORM currency on the player's iDos Games account. Requires only Amount — the price in whole Coin. Like Purchase it is NOT a player resource and never enters ResourceService: it is settled by PlatformCoinPayment in the same transaction as the grant (buyer charged, author credited). Accepted only by the store (Store.Purchase) for now; allowed only in Consume.

ScalarCurveSpec.description: Scalar curve f(base, step): how a value grows with a level, rank, stage or count. THE MODULE'S RULE: an empty field does nothing — an unset curve is the identity f(base,n)=base, an unset bound means there is no bound. All rates are shares (0.1 = +10%), never multipliers, so 0 and empty always mean the same thing.

Base.description: Base the curve is computed from. Empty = use the base supplied by the caller. Fill it only where the base is a publisher setting (a multiplier starting at 1.5, a table's value before its first point) — where the base comes from data (a stat value, a level price, an item bonus) leaving it empty is required, otherwise it overrides the real base.

GrowthRate.description: Compounding rate per step (Shape=Geometric): 0.1 = x1.1 per step. Empty or 0 = no growth.

Interpolation.description: How to interpolate between points. Empty = Step.

MaxResult.description: Upper bound of the result. Empty = there is NO upper bound (not 0).

MinResult.description: Lower bound of the result. Empty = there is NO lower bound (not 0).

PerStep.description: Units added per step (Shape=PerStep). Empty or 0 = no growth.

PerStepRate.description: Share of the base added per step (Shape=PerStepRate): 0.1 = +10% of base per step. Empty or 0 = no growth.

Points.description: Table breakpoints (Shape=Table or TableAbsolute). Empty = no growth.

Shape.description: Curve shape. Empty = Flat, i.e. no growth.

TailGrowthRate.description: Growth beyond the last table point (share per step). Empty = hold the last point's value.

ScheduleChain.description: Recurring phase chain. Holds ONLY chain timing — the phase list lives on the module (a phase composes ScheduleChainPhase + its payload), so the resolver takes a projected IReadOnlyList<ScheduleChainPhase>. Unified replacement of the schedule parts of EventChainDefinition / LeaderboardChainConfig / BoostChainDefinition / CoopEventChainDefinition / SeasonChainDefinition.

AnchorUtc.description: Anchor date (UTC). The first phase of the first cycle starts here; all subsequent dates are computed from the anchor + phase durations + pauses. null = no anchor → the chain is unconfigured and never resolves.

MaxCycles.description: Maximum number of full cycles. 0 = infinite.

PauseBetweenCyclesSec.description: Pause between full cycles (seconds). 0 = no pause.

PauseBetweenPhasesSec.description: Pause between phases inside one cycle (seconds). 0 = no pause.

x-enum-descriptions: Active whenever enabled, no time gate (eternal leaderboard, manual boost).
Single fixed window [StartUtc..EndUtc] (see ScheduledWindow).
Recurring ordered list of phases (see ScheduleChain).
Activated/granted when a source fires (see ScheduleSpec.ActivationTriggers).
Calendar-aligned cycles with reset (see CyclicSchedule).

Window defined RELATIVE to the parent instance's start (see RelativeWindow). Resolved only when a parent is passed to ScheduleResolver.ResolveActive. Enables staged unlocking of sub-entities inside a recurring event (e.g. "Day N opens (N-1)x24h after the current cycle instance start"), so one config auto-repeats without absolute dates.
Every CyclicSchedule.IntervalSeconds seconds from CyclicSchedule.AnchorUtc — a fixed interval, not calendar-aligned (e.g. "every 6 hours" or "every 10 days"). Alignment is defined by the anchor.
No reset — eternal (all-time) instance.

ScheduleSpec.description: "How an entity activates" container, embedded into each system's definition. Exactly one sub-field is filled for the chosen Mode (plus ActivationTriggers for Triggered). Resolved via ScheduleResolver.

ActivationTriggers.description: Sources that cause activation/grant. Required and used only when Mode = Triggered. Matched via TriggerMatcher.

Chain.description: Chain config. Required and used only when Mode = Chained.

Cyclic.description: Calendar-cycle config. Required and used only when Mode = Cyclic.

IsActive.description: Unified global on/off. false = entity paused without deleting config (replaces scattered IsActive/Enabled).

Mode.description: Activation mode. Determines which sub-field is used.

Relative.description: Relative-window config. Required and used only when Mode = Relative.

Scheduled.description: Single-window config. Required and used only when Mode = Scheduled.

ScheduledWindow.description: Single fixed-date window. Unified replacement of the schedule parts of ScheduledEventDefinition / LeaderboardScheduledConfig / ScheduledBoostDefinition.

AllowEarningAfterEnd.description: Whether progress can still be earned after EndUtc (until grace ends). Default false.

ClaimGraceHours.description: Grace window (hours) after EndUtc for claiming rewards. Default 48.

EndUtc.description: Window end (UTC). After this, earning stops unless AllowEarningAfterEnd. null = unset -> the window is unconfigured and never active.

StartUtc.description: Window start (UTC). The entity is active from this moment. null = unset -> the window is unconfigured and never active (BOTH bounds are required).

SegmentGate.description: Unified "who it is available/applies to" gate. Replaces BoostSegmentGate (TimedBoost), MailboxSegmentDefinition filters and StoreOfferRules premium fields. All conditions are AND-ed. An empty/unset field = no constraint on that axis; an empty/null gate = available to everyone. Resolved by SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes.

ActiveWithinDays.description: Active within the last X days (matches Usage.LastActiveAt). 0 = no restriction.

Countries.description: Country filter (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2; matches PublicData.Country, else RegistrationCountry). Empty = all countries.

Experiment.description: A/B experiment condition: the gate passes only if the player is assigned to the required variant (ExperimentVariantCondition). null = not applied. A/B variants thus reuse the whole SegmentGate stack: two configs, each gated to its variant. Assignment is read from UserDataDocument.Experiments (sticky, stable-hash — see ExperimentAssigner).

MaxLevel.description: Maximum Board Rank. 0 = no upper bound.

MinLevel.description: Minimum Board Rank (matches PublicData.BoardRank). 0 = no lower bound.

MinPremiumTier.description: Minimum active premium tier (matches Premium.MaxActiveTier). 0 = no requirement.

Platforms.description: Platforms the entity is available on. Empty/null = all. Unlike the other axes this one comes from the request platform (IGSService.ClientPlatform), not from the player document, and is passed to SegmentGateEvaluator.Passes as a separate REQUIRED argument. The axis is skipped when the platform is Unknown — deliberately soft, because it governs what is shown, not what is charged: payments are guarded by PriceOptionSelector.IsAvailableOn, where Unknown does not pass a non-empty platform list. Not needed to hide entities that simply cannot be paid for on a platform: storefronts already drop whatever has no available price option.

RegisteredWithinDays.description: Registered no earlier than X days ago (new players; matches RegistrationDate). 0 = no restriction.

RequiredPremiumIDs.description: Required active premium IDs (ANY of the list is enough, via PremiumHelpers.GetActivePremiumIDs). Empty = no requirement.

Segments.description: Allowed economy segments (matches PlayerEconomyTuningState.Segment: "F2P","Dolphin","Whale","VIP"). Empty = any.

Tutorial.description: Tutorial condition: the gate passes only if the player is in the required progression state (TutorialGateCondition). null = not applied. By the same trick as Experiment, this gives "after onboarding" gating in every module already using SegmentGate, with no edits to them. To close a whole module there is a cheaper path — TutorialGlobalSettings.Blocking: one check in ClientRun instead of a condition on every entity.

StatDefinition.description: Definition of one upgradable character stat (boost). Specifies upgrade rules: max level, cost, value scaling, requirements. Used in CharacterDefinition.Stats.

AssetPaths.description: Named asset references for the stat (e.g. "icon"). This is the only place stat asset paths live.

BaseStatValue.description: Base stat effect value — the value at level 0, i.e. for an unupgraded stat. This is the base of ValueCurve. Stat levels are numbered from 0 (a missing key in CharacterModel.StatLevels means level 0), unlike prices, item levels and ranks which are numbered from 1.

CostCurve.description: Cost curve over the level. The base is the price configured in PriceOptions; the step is the target level (numbered from 1). Empty = the same price at every level. Leave Base empty — the base is the configured price.

Description.description: Text description of the stat and its in-game effect, for UI.

DisplayName.description: Stat display name for the UI (localized or base).

MaxLevel.description: Base maximum stat level. This is the BASE of CharacterDefinition.StatMaxLevelCurve — the character's rank may raise the cap. The effective value is produced by CharacterConfigResolver.EffectiveStatMaxLevel, the single place where the cap is derived.

PriceOptions.description: Ways to pay per upgrade level. Dictionary key = PriceOption.OptionID; each option's Amount is the base cost for level 1, scaled by CostCurve. A store-paid option is not allowed here: a store SKU is a fixed price tier and cannot follow a per-level formula.

RankCurve.description: Growth curve of this stat over the character's RANK. The base is the stat value at its own level (the result of ValueCurve), the step is the character rank (numbered from 1). Empty = rank does not affect this stat. The former CharacterLevelScalingFactor = 0.05 is Shape=PerStepRate with the same number. This per-stat curve is multiplied by CharacterDefinition.RankStatCurve, which applies to every stat at once. Leave Base empty.

Requirements.description: Prerequisite list. Before upgrading this stat to any level, each listed stat must have reached its required level. Checked in CharacterV2.UpgradeStatLevel before any cost is charged.

StatID.description: Unique stat ID within the character (e.g. "AttackSpeed"). Used as the key in CharacterModel.StatLevels. Must not contain '.' or '$'.

TypeID.description: Stat category — free-form string ID referencing an external title-level catalog of stat types. Defines gameplay role and UI grouping. Same pattern as ItemMetadata.RarityID / CharacterClassification.ClassID: platform does not validate concrete values — this is an extension point for title developers. Recommended (non-binding) values: "Generic", "PrimaryAttribute", "Vital", "Combat", "Resistance", "AttackType", "ArmorType", "Resource". Must not contain '.' or '$' if used in query paths. null = category not specified (legacy-config fallback).

ValueCurve.description: Growth curve of the stat value over the stat's OWN level. The base is BaseStatValue, the step is the stat level (numbered from 0). Empty = the stat does not grow when upgraded. The former StatScalingFactor added units per level — that is Shape=PerStep with the same number; the multiplicative base*(1+f*step) form is Shape=PerStepRate. Leave Base empty.

Weight.description: Stat weight when computing the character's overall combat Power. Higher weight = bigger contribution from this stat.

StatRequirement.description: Prerequisite that the referenced stat must reach the given level. Used in StatDefinition.Requirements and CharacterEquipmentSlot.StatRequirements.

RequiredLevel.description: Minimum level of RequiredStatID needed to unlock the dependent action.

RequiredStatID.description: Dependency stat ID (StatDefinition.StatID) that must be upgraded to RequiredLevel. Must not contain '.' or '$'.

StatsPreset.description: Shared, reusable upgradable-stat set. Stored in CharacterDefinitions.Presets.Stats by PresetID. Structurally identical to inline CharacterDefinition.Stats.

Stats.description: Preset stat directory. Key is StatID. Same shape as CharacterDefinition.Stats.

TriggerSource.description: Unified trigger source: which game event grants progress/grant and under which filters. Replaces EventTokenSource (TimedEvent), LeaderboardScoreSource (Leaderboard) and BoostTriggerSource (TimedBoost). SourceType reuses the existing EventTokenSourceType. Matched via TriggerMatcher.

BaseWeight.description: Base "weight" per trigger: token amount (TimedEvent) or score (Leaderboard). Unifies the former BaseAmount/BaseScore. Unused for TimedBoost triggers (a boost has no quantity).

ChanceOutcomeFilter.description: Only for SourceType = BoardTileLanding on Chance tiles. Whitelist of ChanceOutcome.OutcomeID values. Case-insensitive. Works in AND with TileTypeFilter/TileIndexFilter. Empty/null = not applied.

Limits.description: Anti-farm limits of the source — unified LimitSpec (per-day weight cap DailyWeightCap, per-day trigger cap DailyCap, CooldownSeconds). null = no limits (e.g. leaderboards intentionally apply none).

OutcomeFilter.description: Only for SourceType = BoardAttack / BoardRaid / BoardBuild. Whitelist of outcomes. Empty/null = any. BoardAttack: ["HIT"]/["BLOCKED"]; BoardRaid: ["FINISHED_SMALL"]/["FINISHED_MEDIUM"]/["FINISHED_BIG"]; BoardBuild: ["BUILD"]/["STAGE_COMPLETE"].

Params.description: Context parameters for filtering/identifying the source. CustomAction: {"ActionName":"watch_ad"}. QuestComplete: {"QuestID":"win_5_raids"} and/or {"CycleID":"daily"}. StorePurchase: {"OfferID":"starter_pack"}. MarketplaceSell/MarketplaceBuy: CatalogID / ItemID / OfferType. An unset or empty parameter means "any". Keys not listed here are not checked by the matcher.

ScaleWithRollMultiplier.description: Whether BaseWeight scales with the player's RollMultiplier. true: Weight = BaseWeight x M_roll. false: fixed amount.

SourceType.description: Source type. Identifies which game event fires.

TileIndexFilter.description: Only for SourceType = BoardTileLanding. Whitelist of tile indices. Empty/null = any index. Works in AND with TileTypeFilter.

TileTypeFilter.description: Only for SourceType = BoardTileLanding. Whitelist of tile types (BoardTileType names or CustomTypeID) that fire on landing. Case-insensitive. Empty/null = any tile (not recommended).

TutorialGateCondition.description: "The player finished the tutorial" condition — embedded in SegmentGate.Tutorial exactly as ExperimentVariantCondition is embedded in SegmentGate.Experiment. Thanks to that, tutorial gating works for free in EVERY module already using SegmentGate (Store / DealOffer / Quest / Reward / Leaderboard / ...). This is the per-entity gating level; to close a whole module use TutorialBlockingPolicy, which is cheaper.

FlowIDs.description: Flows whose state is checked. Empty = the condition is not applied (the gate passes). Multiple entries are AND-ed: "after the intro AND after the raid tutorial".

Mode.description: What exactly must hold for those flows. Default Completed.

Negate.description: Invert the condition. Needed for the reverse case — "show this starter offer ONLY to players still in the tutorial". Default false.

SkippedCountsAsCompleted.description: Whether a Skipped flow counts as finished under Mode = Completed. Default true: if the publisher allowed skipping, the skipper must get the same game as the completer.

StepID.description: The step that must be reached. Read only when Mode = StepReached, and applied to every flow in FlowIDs.

x-enum-descriptions: The flow is finished. Default.
The flow is started (in progress or already finished).
A specific step has been reached (TutorialGateCondition.StepID).

value.description: Configuration of the title's character system: the character catalog. Each entry in Definitions is self-contained (own stats, levels, equipment rules).

Definitions.description: Character catalog. Key is CharacterID. The reserved "Main" character must also have an entry here. A character is allowed iff it has an entry in this dictionary.

Presets.description: Registry of shared (reusable) character setting sets (stats / levels / equipment). Characters reference them via CharacterDefinition.Presets. All blocks merge with inline by key: Stats by StatID, Levels by level key, Equipment by SlotID inside Slots. null = unused.
